statements.label: supported
statements.text: SMARCAD1 is enriched across class I and class II ERV subfamilies, most of all at active intracisternal A-type particles, where repressive histone methylation is maintained.
statements.evidence: SMARCAD1 is enriched at ERV subfamilies class I and II, particularly at active intracisternal A-type particles (IAPs), where it preserves repressive histone methylation marks.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this enrichment pattern and the preservation of repressive histone methylation marks at IAPs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Loss of SMARCAD1 blocks the differentiation of embryonic stem cells.
statements.evidence: Here we identify the SWI/SNF-like remodeler SMARCAD1 as a key factor in the control of ERVs in embryonic stem cells.
statements.note: The work is carried out in embryonic stem cells, but the abstract reports only effects on ERV silencing and never mentions differentiation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Removing SMARCAD1 releases the silencing of IAP elements and of the genes next to them.
statements.evidence: Depletion of SMARCAD1 results in de-repression of IAPs and adjacent genes.
statements.note: This is the reported consequence of SMARCAD1 depletion: de-repression of IAPs and of adjacent genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SMARCAD1 and KAP1 need each other to occupy ERVs, and that mutual requirement depends on the ATPase activity of SMARCAD1.
statements.evidence: SMARCAD1 and KAP1 occupancy at ERVs is co-dependent and requires the ATPase function of SMARCAD1.
statements.note: The abstract states that occupancy of the two proteins at ERVs is co-dependent and requires the ATPase function of SMARCAD1.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In senescent cells, L1 elements escape transcriptional repression and switch on a type-I interferon response.
statements.evidence: during cellular senescence, L1 (also known as LINE-1) retrotransposable elements become transcriptionally derepressed and activate a type-I interferon (IFN-I) response
statements.note: This is the central reported finding: L1 derepression during senescence activates IFN-I signalling.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The interferon response belongs to late senescence and helps sustain the senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
statements.evidence: The IFN-I response is a phenotype of late senescence and contributes to the maintenance of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
statements.note: The abstract places the IFN-I response in late senescence and credits it with maintaining the secretory phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Lamivudine given to aged mice downregulated interferon activation and age-associated inflammation in several tissues.
statements.evidence: Treatment of aged mice with the nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor lamivudine downregulated IFN-I activation and age-associated inflammation (inflammaging) in several tissues.
statements.note: Reported directly as the outcome of lamivudine treatment in aged mice.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Inhibiting L1 reverse transcriptase returns senescent cells to active division.
statements.evidence: The IFN-I response is triggered by cytoplasmic L1 cDNA, and is antagonized by inhibitors of the L1 reverse transcriptase.
statements.note: The abstract reports that reverse transcriptase inhibitors block the interferon response, but says nothing about whether senescent cells resume proliferation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Bird genomes carry ERV-derived interferon-inducible enhancers of the same kind.
statements.evidence: lineage-specific ERVs have dispersed numerous IFN-inducible enhancers independently in diverse mammalian genomes
statements.note: The abstract covers mammalian genomes only and neither claims nor denies the same pattern in birds.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting a subset of these ERV elements with CRISPR-Cas9 impaired expression of the interferon-induced genes lying beside them.
statements.evidence: CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of a subset of these ERV elements in the human genome impaired expression of adjacent IFN-induced genes
statements.note: Impaired expression of adjacent IFN-induced genes is the reported effect of the deletions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ERVs have shaped how the transcriptional network behind the interferon response, a major branch of innate immunity, evolved.
statements.evidence: We found that ERVs have shaped the evolution of a transcriptional network underlying the interferon (IFN) response, a major branch of innate immunity
statements.note: This is stated as the study's main finding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The deleted elements turned out to take part in essential immune functions, among them activation of the AIM2 inflammasome.
statements.evidence: revealed their involvement in the regulation of essential immune functions, including activation of the AIM2 inflammasome
statements.note: The abstract names AIM2 inflammasome activation among the immune functions these ERV elements help regulate.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Phylogenetic work placed the root of the KZFP family at a common ancestor of coelacanths and tetrapods.
statements.evidence: we unexpectedly reassigned the root of the family to a common ancestor of coelacanths and tetrapods
statements.note: The abstract reports this reassignment of the family's root as its first result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most KZFPs bind transposable elements, yet most of the elements they target have lost all capacity to transpose.
statements.evidence: we confirmed that the majority of KZFPs bind transposable elements and pinpoint cases of ongoing co-evolution, we found that most of their transposable element targets have lost all transposition potential
statements.note: Both halves are stated: the majority of KZFPs bind transposable elements, and most of those targets can no longer transpose.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Vertebrate species with more transposable elements in their genomes carry more KZFP genes.
statements.evidence: Here, to obtain a global view of this phenomenon, we combined phylogenetic and genomic studies to investigate the evolutionary emergence of KZFP genes in vertebrates and to identify their targets in the human genome.
statements.note: The abstract describes when KZFP genes emerged and what they bind, but makes no comparison between KZFP gene counts and genomic transposable element content.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: KZFPs use evolutionarily conserved fragments of transposable elements as regulatory platforms long after the arms race against those elements ended.
statements.evidence: KZFPs exploit evolutionarily conserved fragments of transposable elements as regulatory platforms long after the arms race against these genetic invaders has ended
statements.note: Stated as the third result: conserved transposable element fragments serve as regulatory platforms once the arms race is over.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Porcine endogenous retroviruses were confirmed to infect human cells, and they were seen moving horizontally between human cells.
statements.evidence: We now confirm that PERVs infect human cells, and we observe the horizontal transfer of PERVs among human cells.
statements.note: Both observations are reported in the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Organs from the PERV-inactivated pigs were transplanted into human recipients without viral transmission.
statements.evidence: Our study highlights the value of PERV inactivation to prevent cross-species viral transmission and demonstrates the successful production of PERV-inactivated animals to address the safety concern in clinical xenotransplantation.
statements.note: The abstract reports producing the animals and frames clinical xenotransplantation as the goal, but describes no transplantation into human recipients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CRISPR-Cas9 inactivated every PERV in a primary pig cell line, and somatic cell nuclear transfer then produced PERV-inactivated pigs.
statements.evidence: Using CRISPR-Cas9, we inactivated all of the PERVs in a porcine primary cell line and generated PERV-inactivated pigs via somatic cell nuclear transfer.
statements.note: This is the reported experimental result, from edited primary cells through to live PERV-inactivated animals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inactivating PERV activity had already been shown workable in an immortalized pig cell line before this study.
statements.evidence: We previously demonstrated the feasibility of inactivating PERV activity in an immortalized pig cell line.
statements.note: The abstract states this earlier demonstration in an immortalized pig cell line.
